# What is Geographic Information System (GIS)?


## Geographic Information System

> A geographic information system (GIS) consists of integrated computer hardware and software that 
> store, manage, analyze, edit, output, and visualize geographic data. (Wikipedia)


:::: {.columns }
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](img/USGS_The_National_Map.jpg)
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {.incremental}

- softwares to handle **spatial data**
- data stored with their **coordinates**
- defined by their **projection systems**
:::

<br>

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}
Two key concepts in GIS:   

- **Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS)**
- data type: **raster vs vector**
:::

:::

## The most commun projection systems

> One system to code them all: [EPSG](https://epsg.io/)^[European Petroleum Survey Group (EPSG) summarizes in a single number the Coordinate Reference Systems which is actually made of a geodetic datums, a spatial reference systems, and an Earth ellipsoids.]

The projection system will depend on the objective and the spatial extent.  

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=45% .fragment}
**Local**  

- France: <br> Lambert 93, conformal conic projection [EPSG:2154](https://epsg.io/2154)
- Europe: <br> Lambert azimuthal equal-area [EPSG:3035](https://epsg.io/3035)
- Other: Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM), e.g. 32N for Western Europe [EPSG:25832](https://epsg.io/25832)
<!-- Polar regions : *prefer azimutal projection* -->
:::

::: {.column width=45% .fragment}
**World**  

- geographic lat/long WGS84 [EPSG:4326](https://epsg.io/4326) used in GPS
- Pseudo-Mercator [EPSG:3857](https://epsg.io/3857) used by GoogleMap, OpenStreetMap, leaflet, ...
- many others (Winkel Tripel [EPSG:53042](https://epsg.io/53042), Robinson [EPSG:54030](https://epsg.io/54030), Mollweide [EPSG:54009](https://epsg.io/54009))
:::

::::

::: aside

ESRI made a long list [here](https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/e8b85d508d2c4f21a3dec4e52dc7d9c4/data) with their properties equal area, equidistant or conformal (= conserve angles).   

:::

## When and why must you care about projection systems?

<br>

#### Crossing multiple spatial data from different sources 

- Keep track of the projection system of your observation data
- Make sure all datasets share the same projection system or project them

<br>


::: {.fragment}
#### Calculating distances, or areas^[`terra` now uses spherical calculation by default using lat/long coordinates]    

- Use appropriate projection system (e.g. equal-area for areas or equidistant for distances)
- The projection system will define the unit

:::

# Two world views: Raster vs Vector

<!-- https://gisgeography.com/spatial-data-types-vector-raster/ -->


## Vector vs Raster data type

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}
### Vector

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
- Points, Lines or Polygons
- Conserve shape and spatial accuracy
- Good for GPS observations, patches, boundaries, ...

:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
- Rivers
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=10}
- Protected areas
:::
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![adapted from <https://sist.pages.in2p3.fr/anf23-geomatique/>](img/vector-raster_sist2023.png){width=100%}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3, .fade-in-then-out .center}
Rivers ?
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=5, .fade-in-then-out .center}
Vegetation index (e.g. NDVI)?
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=7, .fade-in-then-out .center}
Elevation ?
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=9, .fade-in-then-out .center}
Protected areas ?
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=11, .fade-in-then-out .center}
Land use-land cover ?
:::

::: 

::: {.column width="30%"}
### Raster

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
- Matrix, regular grid with equidistant cells
- Spatial resolution = cell size
- Format for satellite data, model output, ...
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=6}
- Vegetation index (e.g. NDVI)
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=8}
- Elevation
:::

::: 

::::

<!-- 
Scale (1/250000) vs resolution (250m, 0.1 degree)
Carefull, opposite to intuition
small scale (1:1000000) = large extent and low spatial resolution
large scale (1:50000) = small extent and high spatial resolution
-->

## Vector vs Raster file format

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}
### Vector

- **Geopackage**(.gpkg) <br> open format based on SQLite
- ESRI shapefile (.shp) <br> historical format from ESRI. <br> Multiple files (dbf, shx, shp, prj)
- GPS Exchange Format (.gpx) <br> XML file designed for GPS data
- geojson (.geojson) <br> plain text file, used in web API but limited to WGS84
- Google Earth (.kml)

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![adapted from <https://sist.pages.in2p3.fr/anf23-geomatique/>](img/vector-raster_sist2023.png){width=100%}

::: 

::: {.column width="30%" .fragment}
### Raster

- **GeoTIFF** (.tif) <br> the standard format. Can store multiple “bands”.
- NetCDF (.nc) <br> for storing multi-dimensional, array-oriented variables
- ASCII Grid (.asc) <br> simple text files
- GRIdded Binary (.grb), WMO standard
- Imagine (.img) ERDAS file format
::: 

::::
<!-- https://www.ecologi.st/spatial-r/gis-data-models-and-file-formats.html -->

# {{< fa brands r-project >}} as a GIS tool

## Is {{< fa brands r-project >}} a good GIS software?


|                  | Desktop GIS (GUI) <br> ArcGIS, Quantum GIS  | Scripting <br> {{< fa brands r-project >}}, Python^[[rasterio library](https://rasterio.readthedocs.io/) is the Python equivalent to `terra`] |
|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------|
| Home disciplines | Geography                | Computing, Statistics |
| Software focus   | Graphical User Interface | Command line          |
| Reproducibility  | Minimal                  | **Maximal**           |


<br>


. . .  


#### {{< fa brands r-project >}} packages

In these tutorials, we will see how to use `terra`, `sf`, and `mapview`.   

Other interesting packages:   

- `mapsf` and `tmap`: creates nice looking maps  
- `exactextractr` : fast extraction on large raster  

Recently deprecated {{< fa brands r-project >}} packages (end of 2023) : `sp`, `raster`, `rgdal`, `rgeos`, `maptools`

## Summary of key functions in `terra`

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}
### Vector

```{.r code-line-numbers="|1-5|7-11|13-14|16-17|19-20|22-23|"}
# read
vector <- vect("my_polygons.gpkg")

# write
writeVector(vector, "my_file.gpkg")

# calculate distance or perimeter
perim(vector)

# calculate area for polygons
expanse(vector)

# calculate distance between objects
distance(vector)

# create buffers around objects
buffer(vector, set_dist)

# find spatially interesecting features
intersect(vector1, vector2)

# transform vector to raster format
rasterize(vector)
```

:::

::: {.column width="30%" .fragment fragment-index=2}

### <>

```{.r code-line-numbers="|1-8|10-11|13-14|16-17|19-21|"}
# coordinate reference system
crs()

# extent of the spatial object 
ext() # (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)

# getting the dimensions of the object
dim()

# making a simple map
plot()

# projection to different CRS
project()

# extract cell values at vector locations
extract(vector, raster)

# remove area outside extent of interest
crop()
mask()
```

::: 

::: {.column width="30%" .fragment fragment-index=1}
### Raster

```{.r code-line-numbers="|1-5|7-8|10-14|16-18|"}
# read
raster <- rast("my_raster.tif")

# write
writeRaster(raster, "my_file.tif")

# resolution of the raster
res(raster)

# decrease the resolution
aggregate(raster, fact = 2)

# change the grid 
resample(raster1, raster2)

# transform into vector
as.line(raster)
as.polygon(raster)
```

:::
